title: Cumulative grammar review
goal: Use all the main A1 grammar together: être and avoir, articles, possessives, adjectives, negation, questions, futur proche and reflexive verbs.

drills.explain: Age uses avoir: il a 25 ans.
nous → sommes (être).
Hunger, thirst, cold and age use avoir: j'ai faim.

drills.text: J'aime ___ café, alors je prends ___ café le matin.
drills.en: I like coffee, so I have (some) coffee in the morning.
drills.explain: Likes use le/la/les (coffee in general); an amount you take uses du.
After a negative, un/une/des become de: pas de voiture.
eau is feminine and starts with a vowel: de l'eau.

items.en: à and de + le / les contractions

drills.en: Tonight I'm going to the movies.
drills.explain: à + le = au.
à + la does not change: à la.
de + les = des.
Before a vowel, use mon even for a feminine noun: mon amie.

drills.text: Karim et ___ femme habitent à Laval.
drills.en: Karim and his wife live in Laval.
drills.explain: femme is feminine → sa. It agrees with the noun, not with Karim.
frère is masculine singular → son, even though Lucie is a woman.
-ien → -ienne in the feminine.
petit goes before the noun and agrees: une petite maison.
grand goes before the noun; appartement is masculine.

items.fr: ne… pas / ne… jamais / ne… plus

drills.explain: ne before the verb, pas after it.

accept: Je ne mange jamais de viande.
drills.explain: ne… jamais = never; after it, de viande.

drills.en: He doesn't live in Montréal anymore.
drills.explain: ne → n' before a vowel: il n'habite plus.
Three ways: intonation, est-ce que, or inversion.

drills.en: What are you doing on Saturday?
drills.explain: Qu'est-ce que = what (as the object).
où = where (with an accent; ou = or).

drills.en: We're going to visit Québec City in July.
drills.explain: nous → allons + infinitive.

drills.prompt: She is going to work tomorrow.
drills.explain: elle va + infinitive.

drills.en: I'm not going to go out tomorrow.
drills.explain: The negation goes around aller: je ne vais pas sortir.
je → me.
nous → nous couchons: the pronoun repeats.
te → t' before a vowel or silent h.

items.fr: Je ne mange pas de viande.
Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire samedi ?
items.en: What are you going to do on Saturday? (to a friend)

steps.title: All of A1 in one email
steps.intro: This email uses almost all the grammar you learned at A1. Read it once for the meaning, then once to spot the grammar.

blocks.title: An email from Vancouver
blocks.context: Mei writes to her friend Olivier in Québec City.
blocks.fr:
Salut Olivier !
Merci pour ton message. Ici, à Vancouver, tout va bien !
Mon appartement est petit, mais il est joli et il n'est pas cher. Il y a une grande fenêtre et un petit balcon.
Le matin, je me lève à six heures et je prends le bus pour aller au travail. Je travaille dans une banque au centre-ville. À midi, je mange une salade et je prends un thé. Je ne mange jamais de viande !
Samedi, ma sœur Lin arrive de Toronto avec ses deux enfants. Ils sont très gentils, mais ils n'aiment pas la pluie ! Nous allons faire une promenade au parc Stanley, et dimanche, nous allons manger au restaurant du quartier.
Et toi ? Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire samedi ? Est-ce que tu as des photos de ta nouvelle maison ?
À bientôt,
Mei
blocks.en: Hi Olivier! Thanks for your message. Here in Vancouver, everything is fine! My apartment is small, but it's pretty and it isn't expensive. There's a big window and a small balcony. In the morning, I get up at six and I take the bus to go to work. I work in a bank downtown. At noon, I eat a salad and I have a tea. I never eat meat! On Saturday, my sister Lin is arriving from Toronto with her two children. They're very nice, but they don't like the rain! We're going to go for a walk in Stanley Park, and on Sunday, we're going to eat at the neighbourhood restaurant. What about you? What are you going to do on Saturday? Do you have photos of your new house? See you soon, Mei

blocks.prompt: Which phrase from the email is a reflexive verb?
blocks.explain: [[se lever]] has the extra pronoun [[me]]: [[je me lève]].

blocks.prompt: Why does Mei write “de viande” and not “de la viande”?
blocks.explain: After a negative ([[ne… pas]], [[ne… jamais]], [[ne… plus]]), [[du / de la / des]] become [[de]].

blocks.prompt: Why “ses deux enfants” and not “sa deux enfants”?
options: Because enfants starts with a vowel
blocks.explain: Possessives agree with the **thing owned**: plural [[enfants]] → [[ses]]. Lin being a woman doesn't matter.

steps.title: Your A1 grammar map
steps.intro: Everything on one page. Use it as a reference whenever you're unsure.

blocks.title: 1. Être and avoir
head: être (to be)
avoir (to have)
blocks.note: **Être**: nationality, job, description, where you are. **Avoir**: age, possessions, family, and [[avoir faim / froid / besoin de]]. Listen: [[ils sont]] has an *s* sound, [[ils‿ont]] has a *z* sound.

blocks.title: 2. Which article?
head: Article
When
Example
rows: J'ai un frère et des amis.
a specific thing, or things in general (likes)
J'aime le café. La banque est fermée.
du, de la, de l', des
Je prends du pain et de l'eau.
after a negative, instead of un, une, des, du, de la, de l' (le, la, les don't change)
Je n'ai pas de voiture. Pas d'eau.

blocks.title: 3. À and de with le and les
head: + le
+ la
+ l'
+ les
blocks.note: Only **le** and **les** combine: [[je vais au parc]], [[le chat des voisins]]. Never write *à le* or *de les*.

blocks.title: 4. Possessives
head: masculine
feminine
plural
blocks.note: The possessive agrees with the **thing owned**, not the owner: [[Karim et sa femme]], [[Lucie et son frère]]. Before a vowel, use **mon / ton / son**: [[mon amie]].

blocks.title: 5. Adjectives
blocks.body:
**Agreement:** add **-e** for feminine, **-s** for plural: [[grand, grande, grands, grandes]]. Some patterns: [[canadien → canadienne]], [[gentil → gentille]], [[sérieux → sérieuse]].

**Position:** most adjectives go **after** the noun: [[une voiture rouge]], [[un ami canadien]]. A few short, common ones go **before**: [[grand, petit, jeune, vieux, beau, bon, nouveau]] — [[une petite maison]], [[un bon café]].

blocks.title: 6. Negation
blocks.body:
[[ne]] before the verb, the second word after it: [[ne… pas]] (not), [[ne… jamais]] (never), [[ne… plus]] (not anymore).

- [[ne]] → [[n']] before a vowel: [[Je n'aime pas]].
- With a reflexive verb, ne goes before the pronoun: [[Je ne me lève pas tôt.]]
- With futur proche, the negation goes around **aller**: [[Je ne vais pas travailler.]]
- In casual speech, people often drop *ne*: [[J'aime pas ça]]. In writing, keep it.

blocks.title: 7. Three ways to ask a question
head: Style
Yes/no question
With a question word
blocks.note: Question words: [[où, quand, comment, pourquoi, combien, qui, quel / quelle]], and [[qu'est-ce que]] (what).

blocks.title: 8. Futur proche
blocks.note: [[je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont]] + infinitive. Nothing goes between them: no *à*.

examples.en: I'm going to take the TEF.
We're not going to work tomorrow.

blocks.title: 9. Reflexive verbs: se lever
head: se lever
negative
blocks.note: [[me, te, se]] become [[m', t', s']] before a vowel: [[je m'habille]].

blocks.title: The ten most common A1 errors
blocks.body:
- [[Je suis 30 ans]] → [[J'ai 30 ans]]
- [[Je suis un ingénieur]] → [[Je suis ingénieur]]
- [[Je n'ai pas des enfants]] → [[Je n'ai pas d'enfants]]
- [[Je vais à le parc]] → [[Je vais au parc]]
- [[sa frère]] → [[son frère]] (masculine noun)
- [[ma amie]] → [[mon amie]] (before a vowel)
- [[une maison petite]] → [[une petite maison]]
- [[Je ne aime pas]] → [[Je n'aime pas]]
- [[Je vais à visiter]] → [[Je vais visiter]]
- [[Je lève à 7 heures]] → [[Je me lève à 7 heures]] (you get yourself up)

blocks.title: Why “j'aime le café” but “je prends du café”?
blocks.body:
With verbs of **liking** ([[aimer, adorer, détester, préférer]]), you talk about coffee **in general**, as a category: [[le café]].

With verbs of **taking, eating, buying** ([[prendre, manger, acheter, vouloir]]), you talk about **some** coffee, an amount: [[du café]].

So: [[J'adore le fromage, alors j'achète du fromage.]] — I love cheese, so I buy (some) cheese.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat the contrasts
blocks.note: In French, a single sound can be the difference between two grammar forms.

lines.fr: Ils sont canadiens. Ils ont deux enfants.
lines.en: They're Canadian. They have two children.
lines.tip: sont = s sound; ils‿ont = z sound.

lines.fr: Il est ici. Il a un chat.
lines.en: He is here. He has a cat.

lines.tip: le = uh, les = é: the article tells you singular or plural.

lines.fr: Je ne vais pas travailler demain.
lines.en: I'm not going to work tomorrow.

lines.tip: Est-ce que = ess-kuh; vous‿habitez with a z link.

lines.fr: Je me lève à six heures.

blocks.explain: You heard a **z** sound: [[ils‿ont]]. Cold uses avoir: [[avoir froid]].

blocks.fr: Je ne vais pas travailler demain.
blocks.en: I'm not going to work tomorrow.
blocks.prompt: Is the speaker going to work tomorrow?
options: Yes, but only in the morning
blocks.explain: [[ne… pas]] around [[vais]]: a negative futur proche.

steps.title: Checkpoint: mixed practice
steps.intro: Ten questions, all mixed up, like real life. Answer without looking at the grammar map, then check what you missed.

blocks.text: Mon frère ___ 25 ans et il ___ ingénieur.
blocks.en: My brother is 25 and he's an engineer.
blocks.explain: Age → avoir ([[il a]]); job → être ([[il est]]).

blocks.text: Le matin, je mange ___ pain et je prends ___ café.
blocks.en: In the morning, I eat (some) bread and I have (some) coffee.
blocks.explain: An amount of something masculine → [[du]]: [[du pain]], [[du café]].

blocks.prompt: How do you say “I don't eat meat”?
options: Je ne mange pas de viande.
Je ne mange pas du viande.
Je ne mange de viande pas.
Je mange ne pas de viande.
optionFeedback: After a negative, use de: pas de viande.
pas goes right after the verb.
ne goes before the verb, pas after it.

blocks.en: Here are my friend Sofia and my parents.
blocks.explain: [[amie]] starts with a vowel → [[mon amie]]. [[parents]] is plural → [[mes]].

blocks.prompt: Match each noun with the right form of gentil.

blocks.explain: Inversion ([[Où habitez-vous ?]]), est-ce que, or intonation ([[Vous habitez où ?]]).

blocks.text: Je vais ___ parc avec les enfants ___ voisins.
blocks.en: I'm going to the park with the neighbours' children.

blocks.prompt: We are not going to work tomorrow.
accept: On ne va pas travailler demain.
Demain, on ne va pas travailler.
Nous n'allons pas au travail demain.
On ne va pas au travail demain.
blocks.explain: [[nous n'allons pas]] + infinitive. [[n']] because [[allons]] starts with a vowel.

blocks.prompt: I get up at seven o'clock.
accept: Je me lève à sept heures
À sept heures je me lève
blocks.explain: Reflexive verb: [[je me lève]]. No être here.

blocks.fr: Ils ont deux enfants et ils sont très contents.
accept: Ils ont 2 enfants et ils sont très contents.
blocks.explain: [[ils‿ont]] (z sound, avoir) vs [[ils sont]] (s sound, être).

blocks.prompt: Reply to Mei's email. Tell her about your home, your morning, what you eat or don't eat, someone in your family, and your plans for Saturday. End with a question for her.
checklist: être and avoir (at least once each)
An article or partitive: le / un / du
A possessive: mon / ma / mes / son / sa / ses
A negative: ne… pas / jamais / plus
A reflexive verb: je me lève…
A plan with je vais / nous allons + infinitive

models.label: Model answer (Olivier)
models.fr:
Salut Mei !
Merci pour ton courriel. Moi, j'habite maintenant dans une petite maison à Québec. Elle est vieille, mais elle est très jolie !
Le matin, je me lève à sept heures et je prends du café avec du pain. Je ne mange pas de céréales : je déteste ça !
Ma mère arrive vendredi. Elle a soixante ans et elle est très active. Samedi, nous allons visiter le Vieux-Québec et nous allons manger au restaurant.
Et ta sœur et ses enfants, est-ce qu'ils aiment Vancouver ?
À bientôt,
Olivier
models.en: Hi Mei! Thanks for your email. I now live in a small house in Québec City. It's old, but it's very pretty! In the morning, I get up at seven and I have coffee with bread. I don't eat cereal: I hate it! My mother arrives on Friday. She's sixty and she's very active. On Saturday, we're going to visit Old Québec and we're going to eat at a restaurant. And your sister and her children, do they like Vancouver? See you soon, Olivier

summary:
- Choose between **être** and **avoir**, and between **le / un / du / de**
- Make possessives and adjectives agree, and use **au / aux / du / des**
- Make negatives, ask questions three ways, talk about plans with **aller + infinitif** and routines with reflexive verbs
